amrDescription: Authentication methods (amr) of which a sign-in must report at least one, for example mfa or hwk. Separate with spaces or commas. Leave empty to require none.
amrEditDescription: The complete list. Separate with spaces or commas. An instance connection must keep at least one.
caBundleClearDescription: Remove the private CA bundle from {{name}}? The provider's certificate will then be checked against the system's trusted roots only, and sign-in through this connection fails if a private CA signed it.
caBundleCreateDescription: Optional. Only for a provider inside your network whose TLS certificate was signed by your own certificate authority: paste the CA certificate (PEM), or choose the file. It is trusted for this provider only, in addition to the system's roots. Certificates only, never a private key.
caBundleDescription: For an on-premises provider whose TLS certificate was signed by your own certificate authority. These certificates are trusted for this provider only, in addition to the system's trusted roots. The server checks a new bundle by reaching the provider with it before saving.
caBundleLooksLikeKeyError: That text contains a private key. Remove it and supply the CA certificate only; keep the key private.
caBundleNone: No private CA bundle. The provider's certificate is checked against the system's trusted roots.
caBundleNotPemError: Expected PEM text with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- blocks.
caBundleRequiredError: Paste or choose the CA certificate (PEM).
caBundleTooLargeError: A CA bundle is up to 64 KiB.
caBundleUnreadableError: That file could not be read.
caBundleVerifyNote: Saving reaches the provider's discovery address using this bundle. If its certificate does not chain to it, nothing is saved. If the provider then names different endpoints than the approved ones, the approval is withdrawn and you review them again.
caCertNotCaHint: This certificate does not say it is a certificate authority. It is trusted as exactly this certificate, which is usually the provider's own certificate rather than the CA that signed it.
callbackUrlDescription: Register this exact address at the provider as the redirect (callback) URI.
claimIncompleteError: Every required claim needs both a name and a value.
claimsCreateDescription: Claims every sign-in must carry with exactly these values. A shared multi-tenant provider must be pinned to your organisation: Google needs hd, Microsoft needs tid.
claimsEditDescription: A Google connection cannot drop hd, nor a Microsoft one tid.
clientSecretDescription: Write-only: sealed in the secret store and never displayed again. Leave empty for a public client.
createdToast: Connection “{{token}}” created. Review and approve its endpoints before enabling it.
deleteDescription: Delete “{{name}}”? This removes the list of tenants it serves (the tenants themselves are untouched), its domains, account links, pending link requests and stored client secret. Memberships it managed are disabled, not removed. People signed in through it lose access at their next token exchange. This cannot be undone.
description: External OpenID Connect providers people sign in through. A connection starts disabled and cannot be enabled until a person has approved the provider's endpoints.
disableDescription: Disable “{{name}}”? Sign-ins through it are refused, and sessions started through it end at their next token exchange. Its settings, domains and links are kept, and you can enable it again.
discoveryDescription: The provider's endpoints as last fetched. Sign-ins use only the endpoints approved here.
dispositionLabel: What becomes of the existing memberships
domainsDescription: Email domains this connection speaks for. Freemail providers and public suffixes are refused, and a domain belongs to one connection.
emailClaimDescription: Name of the claim carrying the person's email address. Leave empty for email.
emptyConnections: No identity providers yet. Create one to let people sign in with their own provider.
emptyDomains: This connection speaks for no domains yet.
emptyLinkRequests: No sign-ins are waiting for a link decision.
enableNeedsApproval: Approve the provider's endpoints before enabling this connection.
instanceNeedsMfaError: An instance connection must require an authentication method, or you must confirm the provider enforces multi-factor sign-in.
instanceServesNoTenants: An instance connection serves no tenants. It reaches an identity only through an explicit account link, and enters a tenant only as a superuser.
issuerDescription: The provider's issuer, an https address. This cannot be changed after the connection is created.
issuerFixedDescription: Fixed when the connection was created.
issuerNotHttpsError: Issuer must be an https address.
kindDescription_instance: The operator's own provider. Linked to identities only by explicit action, and entering a tenant only as a superuser.
kindDescription_tenant: A provider serving one or more tenants' own people. Its sign-ins can enter only those tenants and never reach an identity holding a system role.
linkRequestsDescription: Sign-ins refused because they matched an existing identity with no link. A request grants nothing until you approve it, and approving links the external account to whoever holds that email now.
manualMembershipsHint: Already a member of {{tenants}}, outside this connection. Choose whether the connection takes over those memberships.
mfaAckDescription: Recorded in the audit journal. Only needed when no authentication method is required above.
reapprovalBody: The provider's endpoints changed since they were approved, so sign-ins through this connection are being refused. Review the new endpoints below and approve them to resume.
rejectLinkDescription: Reject the request from {{email}}? It is deleted, and nothing is linked. The person can try signing in again.
removeDomainDescription: Remove {{domain}} from this connection? People with that email domain are no longer sent to this provider at sign-in.
scopesDescription: OAuth scopes to request. Separate with spaces or commas. Leave empty for openid, email and profile.
scopesEditDescription: The complete list of scopes, separated by spaces or commas.
signOutDescription: When someone who signed in through this connection signs out, also send them to the provider's sign-out page. That ends their session at the provider for every application it serves, so leave this off unless your organisation wants it. The sign-out here always completes first, whatever the provider does.
signOutNoEndpoint: There is no approved sign-out endpoint for this provider: either its discovery document has not been approved, or the approved one names none. Signing out ends the session here only. Refresh and approve the discovery document if the provider offers one.
signOutOffToast: Sign-out at the provider turned off
signOutOnToast: Sign-out at the provider turned on
signOutReturnUrlsDescription: Register these exact addresses at the provider as post-logout redirect URIs. The provider sends people back to the console's sign-in page or to the dashboard app.
signOutToggleLabel: Also sign people out at the provider
strandedRefusal: This would leave tenants that require single sign-on with no enabled connection serving them, locking their members out: {{tenants}}. Stop requiring SSO for those tenants, or enable another connection that serves them, then try again.
subjectChangedHint: This identity is already linked on this connection under a different subject, which is what a recycled email address looks like. Approval is refused while that link exists: if you are sure it is the same person, remove the existing link first; otherwise reject the request.
tenantsDescription: Exactly which tenants sign-ins through this connection can enter, and no others.
title: Identity providers
tokenDescription: Letters, digits and hyphens. It appears in the connection's callback address and cannot be changed.
tokenInvalidError: Token may contain only letters, digits and hyphens.
